features.note: index.png and bay-envelope.png both read immediately as an industrial building — column grid, perimeter walls, roof-truss lattice, 2:1 plan proportion. bay-envelope.png (roof ON) reads as a closed rectangular shed with the AHU sitting on top. No ambiguity at any viewing size.

compressor-room.png: solid grey walls form a clear room-within-a-room; the enclosure reads as a thermal boundary, not loose equipment. compressor-room-open.png reveals the interior cleanly — blue receiver cylinder, dark machine boxes, two circular fan openings on the rear wall. The exhaust-wall presets (coupling-exhaust-off/full) show the louver panel on the exterior face. Minor: the large distribution pipe occupies the upper third of compressor-room.png and hides the louver face in that shot; the dedicated exhaust-wall shots compensate fully.

luminaire-grid.png: each luminaire reads as a dark cylinder with a lit white lens at its base — disc UFO form correct, not emissive boxes. Grid regularity is legible: the spacing is visibly consistent. Count at a glance from this end-on perspective: approximately 10, not 18. The trunk duct occludes the left-side column and perspective foreshortening collapses the far rows. The 6x3 layout cannot be confirmed at a glance from this angle. Feature passes on form and regularity; count is the information this shot cannot deliver.

ahu-roof.png: AHU box on roof connects via a cylindrical supply riser that drops through the truss, then meets the trunk duct at the bottom of the frame — air path reads top-to-bottom as one continuous chain, no floating segments. duct-run.png: the riser is the dominant element at left (large shiny cylinder entering the bay), the trunk duct runs the full bay length with green flow arrows, pendant diffusers hang below it. Human figure gives scale. The AHU in ahu-roof.png is a featureless dark box (no fan apertures visible) but blockout primitives are declared correct by spec; the connection geometry carries the read.

compressor-skid.png: the circular cooling-fan grille disc IS present on the front face of each package — the machine signature is modelled. However, the preset lighting is so dim that machine-enamel (#54585c) renders near-black and the packages cannot be distinguished from plain dark crates at a first glance. The grille detail becomes visible on a second look; it does not read at one glance under normal viewing conditions. Answer to the direct question: the packages do NOT read as machines rather than crates at a glance — the darkness defeats the form detail.

important_features.note: The main distribution pipe is a dominant element in luminaire-grid.png and duct-run.png — a large shiny cylinder with green flow arrows running at high level across the bay. Reads immediately as a routed header pipe. Routing is sensible and not cutting through structure.

The tan figure is visible in duct-run.png and luminaire-grid.png. In duct-run.png it reads as a standing person and the 8m clear height is apparent relative to it. In luminaire-grid.png it is very small at the far end of the bay. Does its job in duct-run.png; it nearly disappears in wider shots.

defects.description: The compressor-skid preset is underlit to the point where both packages render near-black against a near-black background. Machine-enamel #54585c is indistinguishable from a plain dark box at this ambient level. The circular cooling-fan grille — the only surface feature that signals 'machine' — requires focused inspection rather than reading at a glance. This is the sole critical-feature failure.

Camera shoots along the bay from the end wall, creating heavy perspective foreshortening. At-a-glance count: approximately 10 luminaires visible, not 18. The 6x3 layout cannot be verified at a glance from this angle. Form (disc + lit lens) and grid regularity are correct; the count is the information this camera position cannot deliver.

The large distribution main pipe occupies the upper third of the compressor-room.png frame and fully occludes the louver/fan face of the enclosure wall. The enclosure still reads as a walled room in this shot, but the exhaust-damper detail is invisible here. The dedicated exhaust-wall presets rescue the feature; this is a shot-composition weakness, not a geometry defect.

corrections.description: Add a targeted fill light in the compressor-skid camera preset — a low-intensity DirectionalLight or boosted HemisphereLight aimed at the skid — sufficient to render machine-enamel #54585c as a mid-dark grey distinguishable from a plain box. The fan-grille geometry is already correct; it only needs enough ambient to be revealed. No geometry changes required.

Adjust the luminaire-grid camera preset from end-on to a 45-degree overhead angle looking across the short axis (3-row axis) of the bay, so the 6x3 grid can be counted in one view without perspective collapse. The trunk duct will remain in the frame but will not occlude an entire column. No geometry changes required.
